description: You can track token copies, their count and the caller's cleanup.

steps.description: tokenize allocates an array of pointers and duplicates input before modifying it. You reset the caller's count through tokenCount.
strtok finds tokens using the supplied delimiter characters. When the pointer array fills, you request twice its capacity and keep the successful pointer in temp.

steps.answer: Each token has its own strdup allocation. The returned pointers refer to those copies rather than the temporary input buffer.
steps.question: Why can the returned tokens survive freeing inputDup?

The output lists eight tokens from This through delimiters. You free each token after printing and then free the pointer array.
